title: Dutch Bros vs. e.l.f. Beauty: Which Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
author: Sara Appino
description: The article compares Dutch Bros and e.l.f. Beauty as investment options in 2026. Dutch Bros, a rapidly expanding drive-thru coffee chain with over 1,225 locations, reported 27.9% revenue growth and improved profitability. e.l.f. Beauty, a digital-first cosmetics company, achieved 24.6% revenue growth with 30 consecutive quarters of sales growth but faces margin pressure from rising costs. The author recommends Dutch Bros for its traffic-driven growth and long runway of new locations, despite e.l.f. Beauty's impressive growth trajectory.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong 27.9% revenue growth, improved net margins (4.9%), successful new location performance exceeding expectations, transaction-driven growth, and recommended as the better buy for 2026 due to long expansion runway and cultural brand appeal.

title: These 2 Retail and Wholesale Stocks Could Beat Earnings: Why They Should Be on Your Radar
author: Zacks.Com
description: The article highlights how the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction) filter can help investors identify stocks likely to beat earnings estimates. Two retail and wholesale stocks are featured: Walmart with a +1.44% ESP ahead of its November 19, 2026 earnings report, and O'Reilly Automotive with a +2.11% ESP before its October 28, 2026 earnings release. Both stocks hold #3 (Hold) Zacks Rank ratings and positive ESPs, suggesting potential for earnings beats.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Walmart has a positive Earnings ESP of +1.44%, indicating the Most Accurate Estimate ($0.65) exceeds the Zacks Consensus Estimate ($0.64), suggesting a higher probability of beating earnings expectations on November 19, 2026.

O'Reilly Automotive has a positive Earnings ESP of +2.11%, with the Most Accurate Estimate ($0.95) exceeding the Zacks Consensus Estimate ($0.93), indicating a strong likelihood of an earnings beat ahead of its October 28, 2026 report.

title: Nike vs. Procter & Gamble: Which Consumer Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
author: Jack Delaney
description: The article compares Nike and Procter & Gamble as investment options in 2026. Nike faces a prolonged turnaround with declining sales and a 44.5% stock decline over the past year, while Procter & Gamble demonstrates strong profitability with an 18.4% net margin and consistent dividend growth. The author recommends Procter & Gamble as the more stable choice for long-term investors, citing its recession-resistant business model and 70-year dividend increase streak, while suggesting investors wait for Nike to show sustained earnings improvements before investing.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Nike is experiencing a prolonged turnaround with declining sales expectations for fiscal 2027, stock down 44.5% over 12 months and 77% over 5 years. The company has a lower net margin (6.7%) and higher debt-to-equity ratio (73%), with the author recommending waiting for multiple quarters of earnings beats before investing.

Procter & Gamble demonstrates strong financial health with 18.4% net margin, robust operating cash flow of $19.5 billion, and consistent profitability. The company is a Dividend King with 70 consecutive years of dividend increases, offers recession-resistant products, and shows steady growth with 7% sales increase in Q3 FY2026. The author explicitly recommends this stock for long-term investors.

title: Dutch Bros vs. Celsius: Which Consumer Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
author: Anders Bylund
description: The article compares Dutch Bros and Celsius as growth stock investments in the shifting beverage market. Dutch Bros operates 1,225 drive-thru locations with 27.9% revenue growth and improving profitability (4.9% net margin), while Celsius achieved 85.5% revenue growth but declining earnings due to acquisitions. Dutch Bros trades at higher valuations but shows better earnings growth, while Celsius offers cheaper valuation and triple the free cash flow but faces heavy Pepsi distribution dependency. The author favors Dutch Bros for its combination of respectable top-line growth and rising profits.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Company shows strong revenue growth (27.9%), improving profitability with net margin expanding to 4.9%, and positive earnings trajectory. Despite higher valuation multiples, the PEG ratio suggests reasonable value when accounting for growth expectations. The author explicitly recommends this stock over Celsius.

While Celsius demonstrates exceptional revenue growth (85.5%) and strong free cash flow ($323.4M), earnings are declining and net margin contracted to 4.3%. The company faces significant concentration risk with Pepsi accounting for 43% of revenue and integration challenges from acquisitions. Cheaper valuation is offset by operational concerns.

title: Investors Heavily Search Walmart Inc. (WMT): Here is What You Need to Know
author: Zacks.Com
description: Walmart has been heavily searched on Zacks.com and has outperformed the S&P 500 with a +10.5% return over the past month. The company shows strong earnings growth expectations (+9.1% for current fiscal year, +12.1% for next year) and has consistently beaten consensus estimates. However, it carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating and trades at a premium valuation (Grade D) compared to peers, suggesting it may perform in line with the broader market in the near term.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: While Walmart demonstrates strong fundamentals with consistent earnings beats, revenue growth of +5.4% for current fiscal year, and outperformance versus the S&P 500 (+10.5% vs +0.7%), the Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating and premium valuation (Grade D) suggest limited upside in the near term. The stock is expected to perform in line with the broader market rather than significantly outperform.
